PC: Obtain key elements of history from available sources (EMS), including the patient’s location relative to fire, type of fire/combustibles, and any testing performed en route (e.g. blood glucose, ECG strips)

Manage ABC’s:
Rapid airway assessment
Cardiac, end-tidal CO2 and pulse oximetry monitoring
Move quickly to intubation and positive pressure ventilation
IV Access with at least 2 large-bore IV catheters
Fluid resuscitation
Expose the patient for a complete survey
Obtain point-of-care and appropriate laboratory and radiographic testing, including blood gases, glucose, carboxyhemoglobin and/or co-oximetery, lactic acid, basic metabolic panel, chest x-ray

Recognize and treat possible carbon monoxide poisoning with $1 0 0 \% \mathrm { F i O } _ { 2 }$ , early consultation for hyperbaric treatment once the patient is stabilized and if such resources are available
Recognize and treat possible cyanide poisoning, using available antidotes (hydroxycobalamin, sodium thiosulfate)
MK: Recognize critical illness in the setting of smoke inhalation
Consider alternate causes for the patient’s mental status and metabolic derangements (other intoxication, sepsis)
